subject: surgery
title: Fogarty Catheter, Buerger Disease and Raynaud Phenomenon

steps.tx: A thin catheter with an inflatable balloon at its tip used to extract clots is the **Fogarty catheter**. Passed beyond the clot through an arteriotomy, the inflated balloon drags thrombus out as it withdraws. It revolutionised emergency embolectomy through small incisions. Overinflating the balloon tears the artery lining, so the balloon is sized by feel as it withdraws through each segment.
steps.say: The Fogarty catheter drags clot out with an inflated balloon through small incisions.

vis.alt: Fogarty embolectomy catheter with balloon tip.
vis.caption: Fogarty balloon embolectomy catheter. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Inflammatory blockage of small limb arteries in young male smokers is **Buerger disease**. Thromboangiitis obliterans causes claudication of feet and hands, progressing to ulcers and gangrene. Complete tobacco abstinence is the only treatment that halts it. Cigarette use only, even without pipe or chewing tobacco stopping, still lets the disease advance to amputation.
steps.say: Buerger disease blocks small arteries in young smokers, and only complete tobacco abstinence halts it.

steps.tx: Episodic white, blue then red colour change of fingers in cold is **Raynaud phenomenon**. Vessel spasm starves the fingers briefly before flow returns painfully. Most cases are primary and benign, though some herald connective tissue disease. Secondary Raynaud phenomenon should be suspected when attacks start after age 40, affect one hand more, or cause digital ulcers.
steps.say: Raynaud phenomenon turns fingers white, blue then red in cold through episodic vessel spasm.

steps.tx: Tissue death from prolonged blood flow failure is termed **gangrene**. Dry gangrene mummifies tissue slowly, while wet gangrene adds infection and spreads dangerously. The line between dead and living tissue guides amputation planning. Wet gangrene smells, discharges and makes the patient septic, so it needs urgent amputation rather than waiting for a line to form.
steps.say: Gangrene kills tissue, dry when mummified and wet when infection spreads dangerously within it.

steps.tx: Choosing where to remove a dead limb segment follows the rule of **amputation levels**. The lowest level with healing blood supply that preserves function is chosen. Preserving the knee joint transforms rehabilitation prospects. Toe pressure and the ankle brachial index guide the level, and a heel that lacks blood supply dooms a below knee stump.
steps.say: Amputation levels choose the lowest healable site, and preserving the knee transforms rehabilitation.

steps.tx: After embolectomy, searching for the clot source is essential, termed **source control**. Echocardiography and rhythm monitoring find cardiac emboli. Anticoagulation prevents recurrence once the source is understood. Atrial fibrillation is the source in most cardiac emboli, and a silent heart attack with mural clot is the next commonest.
steps.say: After embolectomy the clot source is sought with heart imaging and rhythm monitoring.

steps.tx: Once the clot is out, the operation turns to why the limb rebelled and how to stop it happening again. **Vasodilator therapy** eases the spasm that clamps small vessels after embolectomy and in vasospastic disease, warming digits whose arteries are structurally sound but functionally shut. Calcium channel blockers anchor this treatment in Raynaud phenomenon, while prostaglandin infusions rescue critically ischaemic fingers in hospital. The image's lesson is that flow restored mechanically still needs pharmacological protection while endothelium and smooth muscle recover their calm.
steps.say: Vasodilator therapy relieves arterial spasm and protects digits after embolectomy and in vasospastic disease.

steps.tx: Calcium channel blockers ease Raynaud attacks by relaxing vessel spasm, a form of **vasodilator therapy**. Keeping hands warm and avoiding smoking matter as much as drugs. Severe secondary cases may need stronger agents. Nifedipine is the usual first drug, and attacks triggered by beta blockers improve when that drug can be changed.
steps.say: Vasodilator therapy with calcium blockers eases Raynaud attacks alongside warmth and smoking avoidance.

vis.alt: Raynaud attack eased by calcium channel blocker vasodilation with warm reperfused fingers after triphasic colour change
vis.caption: Raynaud attack eased by calcium channel blocker vasodilation with warm reperfused fingers after triphasic colour change. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Young patients with gangrene should prompt thought of unusual causes, grouped as **vasculitis and vasospasm**. Buerger disease, Raynaud phenomenon and autoimmune vasculitis head the list. This differs from atherosclerosis of older smokers. Nailfold capillary loops that are enlarged and dropped out point to connective tissue disease behind secondary Raynaud phenomenon.
steps.say: Gangrene in young patients suggests Buerger disease or vasculitis rather than ordinary atherosclerosis.

steps.tx: Digital sympathectomy is occasionally used for severe Raynaud tissue loss, an operation of last resort called **sympathetic interruption**. Removing sympathetic drive dilates digital arteries temporarily. Results fade with time, so patient selection is careful. Benefit often fades within two years as nerves regrow, which is why it is kept for tissue loss that nothing else relieves.
steps.say: Sympathetic interruption dilates digital arteries for severe Raynaud loss, though benefits fade with time.
